title: Scalable Community Detection Using Quantum Hamiltonian Descent and QUBO Formulation
problem: Community detection in large-scale graph data is computationally expensive with classical optimization; existing approaches lack scalability for diverse graph sizes and structures.
motivation: Efficient community detection is critical for analyzing complex networks and graph data; quantum-inspired methods offer potential speedup over classical approaches.
method: The algorithm reformulates community detection—finding groups of densely connected nodes in a network—as an optimization problem where each node is either in a group or not (a binary choice written as a QUBO, or Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization). It then applies Quantum Hamiltonian Descent, a quantum-inspired optimization technique that finds good solutions by simulating how quantum systems settle into low-energy states. To scale to large networks, the approach uses a multi-level strategy: solving simplified versions of the problem first, then using those results to iteratively refine community assignments across progressively larger sections of the full network.
key_novelty: By pairing a quantum-inspired solver (Quantum Hamiltonian Descent) with a QUBO reformulation of the community-detection problem, the approach can find communities in large networks where classical optimization becomes impractical.
contributions: QUBO formulation of community detection problem amenable to quantum optimization
Multi-level iterative refinement algorithm using QHD
Demonstrates 5.49% better modularity scores with reduced computational time versus classical approaches
primary_theme: Quantum Hamiltonian Descent for scalable community detection
